races.name: Download The At The Races App Handicap Stakes (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Tenadaay
runners_data.note: Returned to form with back-to-back wins at 12f on Standard AW, and the prominent style fits this shape ideally; the 157-day absence is the main query but Fergal O'Brien's return record and a competitive OR=60 suggest she arrives primed for this trip.

runners_data.name: Beggarman
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose best Standard-going efforts have come over 14-16f; Hughie Morrison fires 1 from 4 in the last fortnight and at age 9 the horse needs a generous gallop to land his finishing effort, which this shape may not provide.

runners_data.name: Belle Of Kt
runners_data.note: Three wins in a row including twice on Standard AW, and runs just 3 days ago showing excellent freshness; the prominent style is a natural fit for the expected pace shape here and J S Moore's yard is firing at 4/19 in 14 days — a standout profile for this race.

runners_data.name: Pureis King
runners_data.note: Won twice on Good ground at shorter trips and the Standard AW record (2 runs, 0W) gives limited confidence on this surface; stepping markedly up in trip to 1m5f is an unknown, and with Ryan Kavanagh (3) aboard, the handicap mark of OR=58 offers some theoretical upside if the extra distance suits.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Charm
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner who will set the tempo unchallenged from the gate; Standard AW form at Fireside (2/14f, 3/12f) shows she handles the surface and trip, though the OR=58 and recent form string of 867632 suggests she is at her ceiling and may be caught late.

runners_data.name: Maywedance
runners_data.note: Consistent AW performer with 13 qualifying runs on Standard going, two wins and three places; a true hold-up type who will need the pace to be honest enough to reel in the leaders, but the 3-day turnaround from a previous run and Mason Paetel's (5) light claim add some compensating appeal.

runners_data.name: Belle Amie
runners_data.note: David Simcock's filly has genuine hold-up tendencies shown clearly by her form cycle, but is slotted into a midfield map position because the rear is overcrowded — her natural finishing run may be compromised as a result, even though the Standard-going record (7/12 qualifying runs, 1W4P) is solid.

runners_data.name: Louie's Folly
runners_data.note: Struggled over marathon trips (18f, 22f, 16f) on most recent starts and carries headgear; at heart a hold-up type who finds herself racing in a midfield role she wouldn't naturally seek, and the Fergal O'Brien yard is cold at 0/3 in the last fortnight — limited confidence at this trip and in this shape.

runners_data.name: Into Combat
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott fires with intent (6/26 T14) but Into Combat carries a flagged tendency to fade in the finish, making the hold-up role — already compromised by being mapped to midfield — doubly problematic; AW Standard form shows only one placed effort in nine attempts and recent form of 0-0840 is uninspiring.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Of Charm is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no other natural leader to challenge her, will dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m5f trip on Standard AW ground. With Tenadaay and Belle Of Kt likely to press from prominent positions, the early pace will be measured rather than frenetic, setting up a test of stamina and finishing kick rather than raw speed. Belle Amie, Louie's Folly, and Into Combat are genuine hold-up types by nature but have been mapped to midfield because the rear of the field is already congested — all three are racing at least partially out of role and their finishing kicks may be blunted accordingly. This shape — an uncontested front-runner at a controlled pace with no meaningful pressure — heavily favours prominent-racing types who can travel comfortably just behind the leader and pounce in the straight, making Belle Of Kt and Tenadaay the stylistic beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Of Charm leads uncontested at a steady pace and a prominent tracker consumes her in the straight.
scenarios.body: Sea Of Charm sets a relaxed tempo that rewards horses who travel fluently just off the pace, with the prominent runners conserving energy throughout before striking in the final two furlongs; on Standard going over this trip this shape is a blueprint for prominent types. Belle Of Kt's recent hat-trick of wins and strong Standard-going record make her the primary threat, while Tenadaay's return to form and course-appropriate profile also suits this shape well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays truly moderate and Sea Of Charm is never seriously pressed, conserving enough to repel challengers.
scenarios.body: A controlled, uncontested lead at Lingfield AW over 1m5f with Standard going can allow an experienced front-runner to dictate margins and prove harder to reel in than expected, particularly if the chasing pack is disrupted by positional traffic. Sea Of Charm's recent placed efforts at this course and trip suggest she retains ability when allowed to stride on without interference.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Emerge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace genuinely quickens early enough to string out the field and create a proper stamina test that allows true closers to finish through.
scenarios.body: Under this shape Belle Amie and Maywedance — both holding solid Standard-going records — could pick up ground in the final furlong as the prominent horses tire, though Belle Amie and Louie's Folly are not operating in their natural rear-of-field role here and that tempers confidence materially. Maywedance's strong AW form and consistency at this trip make her the most credible closer in the field if this scenario does materialise.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Pace, Chaos Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If positional jostling between the prominent horses creates an uneven, stop-start pace that scrambles normal running order.
scenarios.body: An erratic tempo would leave Sea Of Charm vulnerable and could shuffle the deck enough to allow a fresh-legged outsider like Pureis King — on seasonal debut at longer distance — or Beggarman to stay on into a minor placing. Into Combat's tendency to fade in the finish and the redistributed hold-up runners operating out of role keep this from being more than a marginal threat to the dominant shape.

watchPoints.text: Belle Of Kt's very short 3-day turnaround means watch for any signs of fatigue or reluctance in the paddock — if she is less than fully bright, her strong favourite profile deflates sharply.

Sea Of Charm wears headgear and has form figures of 867632 — if she is allowed a completely uncontested lead and the pace collapses to a crawl, the prominent and hold-up horses behind her may be caught flat-footed when she kicks early in the straight.

Belle Amie, Louie's Folly, and Into Combat are all natural hold-up types squeezed into midfield roles — watch the start and early positioning to see if any of them are able to drop to the rear naturally, which would improve their chances in Scenario C but the map suggests space will be limited.

Pureis King is stepping up substantially in trip (previously 10-12f, now 1m5f) with only two AW runs on record — a strong gallop that stretches the field would help, and any market support for this unexposed stayer should be noted given the unexplored stamina ceiling.

races.name: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Bands C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Sky Sports Racing 415 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Wyle Cop
runners_data.note: Wins on Lingfield AW at 5f with decent recent form (1/5f/STA), but is a natural hold-up horse pressed into the lead role here due to the absence of any genuine pace-setter; Pierre-Louis Jamin will need to be proactive from the gate, and a STYLE_FIT discount applies given she is racing entirely out of her comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Enter Sandman
runners_data.note: Richard Spencer's three-year-old brings strong course-and-distance credentials — two wins at 5-6f on Standard Polytrack — and the tongue-tie is a positive, but 60 days off the track is a concern; although shown in midfield, his true preference is to race from the rear, meaning his finishing effort depends on a contested pace that may simply not materialise.

runners_data.name: Stock Market
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's gelding has been placed on going similar to today (3/6f/SOF, 2/6f/GOO) but has zero wins or places on Polytrack-style surfaces (0W0P on Standard going in five attempts), and 67 days off adds risk; shown in midfield but genuinely wants to come from off the pace, so the small-field, slow-pace scenario is the worst possible environment for his profile.

runners_data.name: London Is Blue
runners_data.note: Robert Cowell's runner carries top weight of 135lbs and has placed at 5f on Standard Polytrack (2/5f/STA) alongside a course win at 6f on Good, suggesting adaptability; racing from hold-up position but with enough gate speed to track the leader in a four-runner field, Edward Greatrex can position him to pounce without needing a strong pace to reel in rivals.

races.paceDynamic: Wyle Cop, a natural hold-up horse redistributed to the lead role, is the only confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner 5f sprint on Lingfield's Polytrack under Standard conditions, meaning the race will be run at a sustainable, uncontested tempo rather than a pressured gallop. With no genuine front-runner to force the pace, Wyle Cop is likely to bowl along at a comfortable clip, setting up a relatively even-tempo affair that may compress the finish rather than truly test the stayers. Enter Sandman and Stock Market are genuine hold-up types who cannot get to their natural rear position with so few runners, and are shown in midfield as the most realistic compromise — but neither is truly racing in role. This race shape, with a single unhurried leader and a small, bunched field, most favours a horse with early tactical speed who can track the pace closely and respond in the final furlong — a prominent-to-midfield profile benefits most, rather than a true closer who needs a contested pace to reel in rivals.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wyle Cop Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Wyle Cop leads from the outset at a comfortable tempo and is never headed or seriously pressured into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: With no genuine rival to force the pace, Wyle Cop can bowl along in front and dictate a sustainable rhythm, using her position advantage to hold off late challenges in a small field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a rival tracks Wyle Cop closely and delivers a decisive challenge inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A steady early pace gives a close-tracking horse the chance to time a run off the leader's back, with London Is Blue's place form at this course and trip making her the most likely beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is marginally quicker than expected and the midfield runners find daylight to deliver late.
scenarios.body: Enter Sandman has course and distance winning form on this surface and brings the class to capitalise if gaps appear in time, though racing out of natural role limits confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Any Can Win
scenarios.trigger: If the uncontested pace is so modest that the field arrives in a heap at the line with no horse able to establish a clear advantage.
scenarios.body: A race run at a crawl can produce chaotic finishes where raw speed over the last furlong decides matters, giving Stock Market an outside chance if her closing kick translates on the surface.

watchPoints.text: Wyle Cop is a hold-up horse forced onto the lead — watch for signs of greenness or reluctance early from Pierre-Louis Jamin, which could destabilise the race tempo entirely.
Enter Sandman returns after 60 days off track; if he needs the run or is short of peak fitness, his hold-up style becomes even less effective in a race unlikely to set up for closers.

London Is Blue carries 135lbs joint-top weight alongside Wyle Cop in a race of only four runners — weight distribution at 5f on fast Polytrack can stretch a horse's margin for error in close finishes.
Stock Market's Standard-going record (0 wins, 0 places from 3 runs) is a red flag on this surface; monitor market moves to see if connections believe today's conditions are materially different.
With only four runners and a non-specialist leader, the field could arrive in a near-simultaneous finish — watch for draw and stall position to give the first clue about early order.

runners_data.name: Riley Rocks
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard AW going and has Donohoe booked; the 17-day turnaround looks straightforward, but as a true hold-up runner needs either a genuine clip to be set or a late fade from Punchbowl Flyer to land his finishing kick in time.

runners_data.name: Perdy In Paris
runners_data.note: Three places from four starts on Standard AW surfaces underlines course suitability, and de la Sayette is a strong booking; races from the rear so depends on pace being honest, and the step back up from 7f to 6f (without a win) warrants minor caution.

runners_data.name: Kimbara
runners_data.note: Spencer's yard is 3/12 over the last 14 days in form; a genuine hold-up horse whose natural finishing position is at the rear of the field — slotting into midfield here is not where it wants to be, and that positional compromise tempers confidence regardless of ability.

runners_data.name: Logi Bear
runners_data.note: Butler has been busy and productive (6/26 14-day), and Logi Bear has placed over this course and distance on Standard going; however, this horse prefers to race from the back and being funnelled into a midfield slot in a race that already lacks pace is a structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Punchbowl Flyer
runners_data.note: The race pivot — two recent wins over this course and trip, one on this surface, with a tongue tie fitted; runs in front and will be completely unchallenged for the lead, so the quality of its front-running performance will set the template for every other outcome in this race.

runners_data.name: Far Too Fizzy
runners_data.note: Two wins and six places on similar going indicates solid turf AW form for Loughnane's runner, but its true style is hold-up and being pushed closer to the pace than it would naturally choose reduces the chance of producing a clean finish; the 0 from its last run is a flag.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with the most AW miles in the field (headgear: tongue and blinkers); 3 wins on Standard at 6f shows the profile fits the surface and trip, but like the other redistributed horses it races from the rear by nature and midfield is not its comfort zone — experience may offset some of the positional cost.

runners_data.name: Sir Alfie
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent-running rival to Punchbowl Flyer; headgear (tongue) fitted and Greatrex takes the ride, but a form string of 890894 at 6f shows limited ability to convert — its value is entirely tactical, sitting on the leader's girth and hoping for a late collapse rather than winning on raw merit.

races.paceDynamic: Punchbowl Flyer is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 6f Lingfield AW contest and, with no genuine rival pressing for the lead, Alexandra Egan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front — a classic lone-leader scenario on a flat track that historically suits the pace-setter. Sir Alfie is the only other horse with prominent tendencies and will likely slot in behind, creating a straightforward two-tier formation with the bulk of the field in arrears. The hold-up runners — Riley Rocks, Perdy In Paris, and several others — will be chasing from the rear, needing either a strong enough pace or a late fade from the leader to get involved. This race shape clearly favours Punchbowl Flyer and, to a lesser extent, Sir Alfie tracking close to the action; genuine hold-up horses face a stiff ask if the pace is modest and the leader idles to the line. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Kimbara, Hierarchy, Logi Bear, and Far Too Fizzy are all true hold-up horses redistributed to midfield, and in reality several will struggle to find their natural rhythm, further reducing their prospect of landing a meaningful late challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Punchbowl Flyer Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Punchbowl Flyer dictates an uncontested lead at a honest but manageable pace and kicks clear in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Egan settles the veteran at the front unchallenged, finding a rhythm that suits a 9-year-old who has won twice at this course and trip; with no rival able to apply pressure, the pace is entirely on Punchbowl Flyer's terms and the hold-up brigade are left with too much to do. Sir Alfie, tracking in second, is the most likely beneficiary if the leader ties up late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sir Alfie Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Punchbowl Flyer sets a genuinely strong pace and ties up inside the final furlong, allowing Sir Alfie to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Sir Alfie's prominent position just off the leader's shoulder becomes a potent tactical weapon if the gallop proves too hot for a nine-year-old to sustain all the way; Greatrex can switch the momentum once the leader weakens. Riley Rocks, closing from further back, is the next most likely to benefit if the race truly falls apart for the front two.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to string the field out and a genuine closer picks off the principals in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Riley Rocks is the strongest candidate given an OR-72 rating, a course-and-distance win on Standard going, and Donohoe's ability to produce a late run; Perdy In Paris, placed three times on this surface, gives the scenario a second live option. This shape requires the pace to be truly honest — a modest lead from Punchbowl Flyer makes it considerably less likely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If a slow-to-develop pace causes the field to bunch and hold-up horses trapped in traffic fail to find a clear run.
scenarios.body: Redistribution of multiple hold-up horses — Kimbara, Hierarchy, Logi Bear, Far Too Fizzy — into midfield creates a congested pack that benefits no one racing out of role; the result could be a messy finish where shorter-priced runners underperform. Hierarchy, with the most AW experience in the group, carries the best chance of threading through if gaps appear late.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Punchbowl Flyer is allowed to dictate a true or false pace — if Egan slows the gallop through the first two furlongs, the hold-up runners will have no chance of closing and the leader's chance rockets further.

Sir Alfie's tendency to race prominently means Greatrex may push forward early; if he applies any pressure to Punchbowl Flyer in the first furlong, the dynamic shifts and the race becomes harder to read.

With Kimbara, Hierarchy, Logi Bear, and Far Too Fizzy all crowding the midfield despite being natural hold-up types, traffic congestion between the 2f and 1f pole is a live risk — watch for horses getting boxed in or switching wide late.

Riley Rocks is the one hold-up horse with proven course form on this exact surface and trip; monitor its position at halfway — if Donohoe secures a clear passage on the outside by the 2f pole, it becomes the main danger to the leader in the closing stages.

Perdy In Paris has not won in four attempts on Standard AW going despite placing three times — watch whether it finds the same limitation in the final furlong, suggesting a horse that gets into contention but consistently finds one too good.

races.name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Borderline Madness
runners_data.note: Best AW form shows she can be competitive on standard going (1st and 2nd in last five on STA), but William Stone's yard is out of form (0/5 last 14 days) and 92 days off is a significant concern; a genuine deep hold-up horse whose redistributed midfield position dilutes her chance in what shapes as a front-runner's race.

runners_data.name: Equion
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's in-form yard (5/45 last 14 days) offers stable confidence, and an 8-year-old with consistent AW placed form, but this runner's natural hold-up style is compromised by the lack of true pace to chase; mapped to midfield but unlikely to get far enough forward to strike.

runners_data.name: Makes Me Wonder
runners_data.note: David Simcock sends this 4-year-old back for another attempt, but an 0W0P similar-going record and a form string dominated by mid-table finishes paint a difficult picture; runs from hold-up but the steady pace scenario this race produces is the worst possible canvas for a closer with no proven finishing kick.

runners_data.name: Wrist Art
runners_data.note: Just four days since last run is the standout flag here — connections are clearly keeping this 9-year-old fit and sharp, and a placed effort over this exact 12f trip on standard going is relevant; a true hold-up runner by style, but placed at 12f recently and could benefit if the front two capitulate late.

runners_data.name: Monks Mead
runners_data.note: The sole genuine prominent type aside from the leader and brilliantly placed to sit second wheel throughout; Luke Morris's positional judgment is an asset, 1W4P on similar going shows competitive consistency, and 11 days between runs suggests freshness without staleness.

runners_data.name: Pure Theory
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who dictates the pace on what will be a Standard AW surface that suits controlled front-running; apprentice Oliver Carmichael (7lb claimer) helps with the weight, though an 0W0P similar-going record and a recent form string of 690056 demands significant improvement to convert control into victory.

runners_data.name: Sansanetti
runners_data.note: Highest OR in the field at 59, and a course-and-distance winner on standard going makes this Pat Cosgrave booking meaningful; races from hold-up but the modest gallop means he'll need to be assertive from his midfield berth — Stuart Williams has 3 winners from 32 runs last 14 days suggesting stable is ticking over.

runners_data.name: Sceptic
runners_data.note: Won on standard going over 8f in recent form (1st in last five on STA, also placed on GOO) and Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim is useful at this level; a natural hold-up runner repositioned in midfield, but of all the closers in this race he has the most compelling AW form profile to mount a challenge if given any daylight in the straight.

races.paceDynamic: Pure Theory is the lone confirmed front-runner and will lead from the outset on this flat Lingfield AW 1m2f circuit, setting a sustainable and uncontested gallop that is unlikely to be pressured into anything uncomfortable. Monks Mead, the one genuine prominent type, will sit just off the leader and shapes to track comfortably in second, meaning the early sectionals should be controlled and measured rather than truly searching. With no second front-runner to apply pressure, the pace is likely to be modest through the first half of the race, compressing the field and making it harder for hold-up horses to generate meaningful momentum late. This race shape overwhelmingly favours horses racing on or near the pace — Pure Theory and Monks Mead are best positioned to exploit the steady early fractions, while the hold-up contingent faces a compressed finish on a track that already rewards handy runners. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the race can accommodate at the rear; Borderline Madness, Equion, Makes Me Wonder, Wrist Art, Sansanetti and Sceptic are all natural hold-up horses, but only those who can push forward from their redistributed midfield positions — most plausibly Sceptic and Sansanetti given their class and recent form — are likely to be close enough to pounce if the pace collapses late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pure Theory Controls Wire-To-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Theory bowls along in front unchallenged and Monks Mead fails to close the gap rounding the home turn.
scenarios.body: Pure Theory's uncontested lead sets a gentle tempo that allows it to conserve energy and kick clear inside the final furlong before the hold-up pack can wind up; this is a classic front-runner's gift on a flat track with no pressure applied.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Poacher Collars Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Monks Mead tracks Pure Theory throughout and powers past inside the final furlong with a superior cruising speed.
scenarios.body: Monks Mead's prominent style is perfectly suited to sitting a length off an uncontested leader and timing a run that negates the finishing kick of those coming from deeper; Luke Morris's positional awareness is a key asset here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Swamps Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is slow enough to bunch the field and a hold-up runner generates enough momentum from midfield to catch the leaders flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A truly slow pace can paradoxically gift hold-up horses an opportunity if the front two tie up in a sprint finish; Sceptic, with a recent course win at the trip and strong standard-going form, and Sansanetti, highest-rated in the field, are best equipped to produce a late thrust from the pack.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Fold, Chaos Erupts
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Theory and Monks Mead fade badly in the final two furlongs after a sustained effort and the race opens up for a surprise hold-up winner.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the front-runners to have overcooled from their uncontested position — possible if the deceptively flat track conceals hidden stamina demands; Borderline Madness, whose best form came from behind, and Wrist Art, placed over this trip recently, could capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Pure Theory's front-running effectiveness depends entirely on Monks Mead not applying immediate pressure — if Luke Morris elects to sit close and force a genuine gallop, Pure Theory's stamina reserves may be exhausted before the home turn.

Sceptic's course-winning form and Ryan Kavanagh's claim make him the most dangerous closer in the race — watch whether he can push forward from his redistributed midfield position early enough to be in contention rounding the final bend.

Wrist Art ran just four days ago; connections clearly believe he is at his peak, but a 9-year-old asked to back up quickly on soft-ish schedules can fade sharply in a late sprint — monitor his energy in the straight.

With six of eight runners being genuine hold-up types crammed into midfield, the home straight could see significant traffic problems — those drawn widest or with jockeys who push through early (Cosgrave on Sansanetti) will have a material positional advantage in the bunched finish.

Pure Theory wears a hood (hg:p) which may settle him through the early furlongs — if the headgear keeps him relaxed under no pressure, the combination of controlled fractions and a fresh apprentice booking could be more potent than the bare form figures suggest.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fallacious Promise
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in good recent form (two wins from six, including a course win at this trip on AW Standard), trainer John Butler in solid 14-day form at 6/26, and last ran just five days ago — freshness is not a concern but recovery merits monitoring; the key question is whether Shamacid's slow pace gives enough time for this closer to reel him in.|

runners_data.name: Mbappe
runners_data.note: Won over this course and trip on Standard going but arrives after 31 days off with headgear noted; a true hold-up type displaced to midfield on the map because this field is stacked with closers, meaning he is unlikely to find his ideal position and his STYLE_FIT flag of 0.91 tempers confidence in a scenario that demands late space.|

runners_data.name: Chapman's Peak
runners_data.note: Won on debut but has returned placings of 8-8-7 since that win, suggesting a horse finding its level; experience on Standard AW going is limited (2W2P from 9 runs) and the step back to 8f from recent 7f runs may help — Ed Dunlop's 14-day strike rate (1/18) is modest.|

runners_data.name: Credit Forgedd It
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave takes the ride on a horse whose last five runs include a win at 8f on Good and a placed effort, but zero wins on AW Standard; though listed as a hold-up horse, the map places him in midfield because so many closers can't all get their preferred position — Simon Dow's stable is quiet (0/8 in 14 days), which adds caution.|

runners_data.name: Dark Rosa
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who has struggled for consistency (form string 579836) and arrives off 25 days, with all five of her last runs coming on Good or Standard turf equivalents — course stats are modest (1W1P from 15 runs); Rose Dawes' 5lb claim is a potential edge if she can hold Shamacid's slipstream without over-committing.|

runners_data.name: Shamacid
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose entire recent profile (14 AW Standard runs, 0 wins but 8 placings) screams a horse that performs consistently in this role without converting; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim helps the weight and the absence of any pace rival means he can set a frugal tempo — this is his race to control even if his strike rate suggests he may be caught late.|

races.paceDynamic: Shamacid is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner mile handicap on Lingfield's all-weather surface and should lead from the gates without any meaningful pressure, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop that is unlikely to be seriously contested. Dark Rosa is the only other horse with a prominent profile but has shown little inclination to dominate, meaning Shamacid can dictate terms comfortably from the front. The remainder of the field — Fallacious Promise, Chapman's Peak, Mbappe, and Credit Forgedd It — are all hold-up types, with Mbappe and Credit Forgedd It redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more genuine closers than the race shape has room to accommodate at the rear; in practice, neither is likely to secure a truly advantageous position. This race shape — a lone, unhurried pace-setter controlling a modest tempo with a wall of hold-up horses in behind — most favours a confirmed front-runner or a horse capable of sitting just off the pace and kicking early, as the pack is likely to find the fractions deceptively slow before the sprint home proves competitive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Shamacid Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Shamacid bowls to the front unchallenged and sets a moderate, metronomic gallop that suits a controlled front-runner.
scenarios.body: Shamacid dictates every yard, keeps the tempo honest but not burning, and forces the field to come to him in the straight; with no rival willing to challenge early, he gets an uncontested lead that is difficult to peg back on Lingfield's polytrack. This shape firmly benefits the front-runner and any horse capable of tracking closely, as the hold-up brigade are left with too much to do against a winner who never relinquishes the initiative.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly slow and the pack bunches, allowing a horse with a strong late turn of foot to pick them all off in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Fallacious Promise, the form pick among the closers, times a run from off the pace to cut down Shamacid close home as the slow gallop compresses the field; Chapman's Peak, who has won over course and distance, could also find room to finish powerfully if the fractions suit. This shape is feasible but relies on the closers getting the run of the race — given redistribution issues, genuine hold-up positioning is compromised.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Dark Rosa gets a slipstream just off the leader and produces a decisive kick rounding the home turn.
scenarios.body: Dark Rosa tracks Shamacid in second or third, saves energy in a slowly-run race, and uses the prominent position to strike earlier than the hold-up pack can respond; with a 5lb claimer aboard in Rose Dawes, there is a risk of mistiming, but if executed well this is a potent position in this shape. This scenario rewards horses with tactical pace who can fire from close to the action rather than grinding from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Shamacid weakens dramatically inside the final two furlongs and the race dissolves into a sprint for the line from all angles.
scenarios.body: A messy finish unfolds as Shamacid stops, leaving the hold-up horses with a wall of traffic to navigate, and the result becomes a scramble; Mbappe and Credit Forgedd It, though displaced from their natural rear-of-field berth, could benefit if gaps appear, but their STYLE_FIT concerns mean this is the least reliable scenario for them. This outcome is the lowest-probability shape given Shamacid's solid AW record and the absence of any horse likely to push him beyond his limits early.

watchPoints.text: Shamacid is the sole pace-setter and if he gets his own way unchallenged in front, no one in this field has an obvious mechanism to force him off his rhythm — watch whether he is allowed to stride clear turning for home before the hold-up pack can organise.
Fallacious Promise ran just five days ago; if any fatigue shows in the closing stages after a quick turnaround, it transforms the race shape and removes the most credible closer from the contest.

Mbappe and Credit Forgedd It are true hold-up types mapped to midfield — watch at the start and into the first bend to see whether they settle further back than shown, which would stretch their task considerably given a controlled pace.

Dark Rosa with Rose Dawes (5lb claim) is the only prominent-style horse capable of sitting close to Shamacid — watch whether Dawes elects to track the leader or drops in behind the midfield group, as that tactical decision fundamentally shapes the race outcome.

Chapman's Peak's last three AW runs have produced 7th, 8th, and 8th — watch whether there is any market confidence at the off that suggests connections believe this trip and surface are now working in his favour.
